name: Osmind vs Valant
title: Osmind vs Valant: Psychiatry EHR Comparison (2026)
description: Compare Osmind and Valant for psychiatric practices. See differences in e-prescribing, outcome tracking, treatment-resistant depression support, and which EHR is best for psychiatrists.

summary.bottom_line: Osmind is purpose-built by psychiatrists for outpatient psychiatry, with documentation templates that mirror actual psychiatric assessment workflows—ideal for practices offering ketamine, TMS, or treatment-resistant protocols. Valant serves broader behavioral health organizations with stronger analytics and outcome tracking for larger teams.

sections.heading: Osmind vs Valant: Overview
sections.content: Osmind and Valant are both EHR platforms serving psychiatrists, but they target different practice types and have different origins. Osmind was built by psychiatrists, for psychiatrists—its documentation templates mirror how psychiatric assessment actually unfolds, and it's particularly strong for practices offering treatment-resistant depression protocols like ketamine infusion and TMS. Valant is a broader behavioral health EHR designed for larger organizations that prioritize analytics, outcome tracking, and standardized data capture.

sections.heading: Documentation & Clinical Workflows
sections.content: Osmind's templates were designed by practicing psychiatrists to match real clinical workflows. The platform uses validated psychiatric instruments clinicians already rely on, and e-prescribing is built specifically for controlled substance workflows common in psychiatry. Valant takes a checklist-style approach with standardized fields designed for consistent data capture across larger teams. Many psychiatrists find Osmind more intuitive for their specific workflow; Valant's structure is better for organizations needing standardization across multiple providers.

sections.heading: Treatment-Resistant Depression Support
sections.content: Osmind has a clear advantage for practices offering ketamine infusion, TMS (transcranial magnetic stimulation), or other treatment-resistant depression protocols. The platform was specifically designed to support these emerging psychiatric treatments with appropriate documentation, monitoring, and protocol management. Valant can document these treatments but lacks Osmind's specialized support and workflows for interventional psychiatry.

sections.heading: Outcome Tracking & Analytics
sections.content: Valant is stronger for organizations that prioritize outcome measurement and reporting. It offers robust analytics dashboards, configurable clinical workflows, and tools for tracking patient progress across larger practices. This is valuable for value-based care arrangements or organizations needing to demonstrate treatment effectiveness. Osmind includes built-in measurement tools using validated instruments but doesn't match Valant's analytics depth for larger organizations.

You run a larger behavioral health organization with multiple providers, you need robust outcome analytics and reporting dashboards, you prioritize standardized data capture for team-based care, or you're in value-based care arrangements

faqs.q: Is Osmind or Valant better for solo psychiatrists?
faqs.a: Osmind is generally better for solo psychiatrists. It was built by psychiatrists with documentation templates that match actual psychiatric workflows. Valant is designed more for larger organizations with team-based workflows and analytics needs.

faqs.q: Which supports ketamine and TMS practices better?
faqs.a: Osmind has clear advantages for ketamine infusion and TMS practices. The platform was specifically designed to support treatment-resistant depression protocols with appropriate documentation, monitoring, and workflows. Valant can document these treatments but lacks Osmind's specialized support.

faqs.q: Do both Osmind and Valant support e-prescribing for controlled substances?
faqs.a: Yes, both platforms support e-prescribing including EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances). Osmind's e-prescribing was built specifically for controlled substance workflows common in psychiatry. Valant offers integrated PDMP lookups in the prescribing workflow.

faqs.q: Which has better outcome tracking: Osmind or Valant?
faqs.a: Valant has stronger outcome tracking and analytics capabilities with robust reporting dashboards. This is particularly valuable for larger organizations or value-based care. Osmind includes measurement tools using validated psychiatric instruments but focuses more on clinical workflow than analytics.
